title: Find the Lexicographically Largest String From the Box I
summary: Given a string word and an integer numFriends, Alice organizes a game for her friends.
statement: Given a string word and an integer numFriends, Alice organizes a game for her friends. In each round, word is divided into numFriends non-empty parts uniquely. All parts are placed in a box. Determine the lexicographically largest string found in the box after all rounds.
constraints: word has 1–5,000 lowercase letters and 1 <= num_friends <= len(word).
Across all splits into num_friends nonempty consecutive parts, every produced part is placed in the box.
Return the lexicographically largest part that can appear.
hints: A part beginning at any index can use at most n-numFriends+1 characters.
For every start, take its longest feasible slice; a shorter prefix cannot beat its own longer version.
Special-case one friend, then return the maximum slice word[i:i+limit].
Every feasible part is a prefix of one candidate slice, and lexicographic order favors the candidate when that prefix ties.
editorial: Every feasible part is a prefix of one candidate slice, and lexicographic order favors the candidate when that prefix ties.

tests.explanation: The prefix dbc can appear while leaving a for the second friend, and it is lexicographically largest.
With one friend the only part is the full word.
